"Oso" Ighodaro''' (born July 14, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. ==Early life and high school career== Born in [[Mesa, Arizona]], Ighodaro grew up in [[Chandler, Arizona|Chandler]] and attended [[Desert Vista High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2019/09/19/get-know-2020-marquette-commit-oso-ighodaro/2369265001/|title=Get to know: 2020 Marquette commit Osasere 'Oso' Ighodaro|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=September 19, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2023}} He averaged 10 points, six rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/marquette-recruiting-q-a-2020-forward-osa-ighodaro/1974591001/|title=Marquette recruiting Q&A: 2020 forward Osa Ighodaro|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=August 10, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2023}} Ighodaro was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]].{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2019/09/13/marquette-basketball-recruiting-commitment-forward-osasere-ighodaro/2312860001/|title=Marquette basketball gets commitment from forward Osasere Ighodaro|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=September 13, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2023}} ==College career== Ighodaro played in five games during his true freshman season with the Marquette Golden Eagles before suffering an injury and using a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2022/11/07/marquette-basketball-coach-shaka-smart-will-use-oso-ighodaro-as-passer/69616098007/|title=Oso Ighodaro barely played as a freshman for Marquette. Two years later, Shaka Smart ready to empower him with big role.|first=Ben|last=Steele|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=December 1, 2023}} He played in all 32 of Marquette's games and averaged 5.5 points per game during his redshirt freshman season. Ighodaro spent the following summer practicing to improve his passing and ball handling skills at the recommendation of coach [[Shaka Smart]] so that he could be a better fit in the Golden Eagles' starting lineup.{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/4083815/2023/01/12/marquette-win-uconn-oso-ighodaro/|title=‘Unique’ Oso Ighodaro is Marquette’s most valuable asset in win over UConn|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=January 12, 2023|access-date=December 1, 2023}} As a redshirt sophomore he was named second team [[List of Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East Conference]] after averaging 11.4 points, a team-high 5.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 1.5 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/news/ten-potential-college-basketball-breakout-stars/|title=Ten potential college basketball breakout stars|first=Jamie|last=Shaw|website=On3.com|date=August 18,
